bull_case: MELI is becoming a regional digital operating system spanning marketplace, logistics, payments, savings, credit and advertising. Cross-ecosystem engagement is still accelerating at mainstream scale.
bear_case: The model may increasingly resemble capital-intensive scale execution rather than fresh disruption. Banks, Nubank, Amazon, Shopee and local specialists can attack individual layers while credit and logistics dilute returns.
thesis: MELI remains a proven disruptive platform rather than a narrative-stage innovator. Commerce and fintech adoption are mainstream, and ecosystemic users show materially higher engagement than single-vertical users. Credit, ads and payments create monetized adjacent value pools. The remaining constraint is economics: credit-card NIMAL is negative and logistics/credit investment is suppressing current cash conversion.

evidence.claim: Q2 2026 fintech MAUs reached 88M and unique active buyers 89M; GMV was $21.9B and TPV $101B.
Ecosystemic users grew 37% YoY and generated 70% more GMV per user than marketplace-only users; MELI+ subscribers grew 72% YoY.
The credit portfolio exceeded $16B, up 75% YoY, while total fintech MAUs and AUM continued to scale across core markets.
Advertising net revenue grew 73% YoY in USD, demonstrating a monetized adjacent value pool built on marketplace demand and seller data.
Consolidated NIMAL was 20.7%, but credit-card NIMAL was -2.5% in Q2 2026, showing that adoption is proven while some newer financial products still require economic maturation.

counterevidence: Individual layers face well-capitalized competitors including banks, Nubank, Amazon and Shopee.
Credit growth increases capital intensity and exposes the ecosystem to underwriting and funding cycles.
Free-shipping and logistics investment can improve adoption while depressing near-term margin and cash conversion.
At current scale, part of the original disruption has already become incumbent execution.
unknowns: Long-run contribution margins of credit cards after acquisition and funding costs.
Independent market-share data across commerce, acquiring and digital banking in each core country.
Long-run incremental ROIC of logistics, MELI+ and advertising as the ecosystem matures.
falsifiers: Cross-ecosystem users stop showing better engagement/economics than single-vertical users.
GMV/TPV growth converges to market while margins and adjusted FCF remain depressed.
Credit or logistics scale destroys enough capital efficiency that adjacent value pools no longer add economic value.

key_kpis.name: Ecosystemic user growth
key_kpis.threshold: remain the fastest-growing user cohort with superior engagement

key_kpis.name: GMV / TPV / fintech MAUs
key_kpis.threshold: sustain structural outgrowth in core markets

next_checks: Track credit-card NIMAL and NPL as portfolio growth continues.
Track ads and MELI+ monetization versus incremental acquisition/logistics cost.
Compare commerce and fintech share trends with major local competitors.

subscores.rationale: Integrated marketplace, logistics and fintech materially replace fragmented regional workflows and change convenience/cost structure. The score stops below 90 because a universal 10x economic advantage is not established.
Usage is mainstream at tens of millions of buyers and fintech MAUs, with GMV and TPV still growing above 40%-50%. This meets the 90 mainstream-adoption anchor.

At least three monetized adjacent pools—payments/acquiring, credit/savings and advertising/subscription/logistics services—are integrated around the regional marketplace, and MELI effectively defines the cross-vertical ecosystem standard in core markets.

uncertainties.rationale: Customer behavior change is clear; the precise cost advantage versus each local alternative is less standardized.
Adoption is well established; the primary question is profitability rather than usage.
Well-funded competitors can attack individual verticals even if replicating the whole ecosystem is harder.
